clients.title: Connect an app
clients.intro: This vault speaks the Bitwarden protocol, so their apps work with it.
clients.setUpFirst: Set your vault up first. There is nothing for an app to sign in to yet.
clients.signInHint: On the app's sign-in screen, choose self-hosted and paste this in. Sign in with the address on your Polaris account and your master password.
clients.insecure: This address is not HTTPS. Most clients refuse to sign in over a plain connection, and they are right to - set up a certificate under Management > Domains first.
clients.extensionHint: Open it, press the settings cog on the sign-in screen, pick "Self-hosted" and paste the address into Server URL.
clients.desktopHint: Tap the region selector above the email field, choose "Self-hosted", and paste the address into Server URL.
clients.cliHint: Point the CLI at this server, then sign in as usual.
clients.letInOne: Polaris' own extension does not ask for your master password. It shows a code, you approve it here in a browser that already has this vault open, and it is handed a copy of the vault key sealed so that only it can open it.
clients.letInTwo: It opens this screen for you. Open it yourself if the extension could not, and type the code it is showing.
clients.ownOne: Built for this vault rather than adapted to it: it asks the browser for permission to talk to this address and no other, fills a login without holding any standing access to the pages you open, and locks itself again when you stop using it.
clients.ownTwo: The package for your browser is under Downloads, with the desktop app and everything else installable.
clients.signedInTitle: Apps signed in to this vault
clients.noneSignedIn: Nothing has signed in yet. An app appears here the first time it does.
clients.claimNote: The name and the kind are what each app said about itself, not something Polaris checked. If you do not recognise one, change your master password: removing a row cannot shut out something that already holds the vault key.
clients.separateTitle: If an app asks for each address separately
clients.separateHint: Some versions offer a custom environment with a field per service. These are the values.
clients.differentOne: Accounts are made in Polaris, not from a client - an app's "create account" will be refused, and your master password is separate from the one you sign in to Polaris with.
clients.differentTwo: Two-step login uses the authenticator on your Polaris account, so a code from it is what an app will ask for.
clients.differentThree: Icons for saved sites are fetched by this server rather than by Bitwarden, so the list of sites you have accounts on stays here.
clients.trademark: Bitwarden is a trademark of Bitwarden, Inc. Polaris is not affiliated with them; it implements their published client protocol.
